title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: functional time series sequence curves observed time, age-specific death rates successive years. dependence curves decays slowly, series long memory. functional autoregressive fractionally integrated moving-average (FARFIMA) model describes series. curves XtX_t fractionally differenced short-memory curves YtY_t, ∇dXt(u)=Yt(u),∇=1−B,\nabla^d X_t(u) = Y_t(u), \qquad \nabla = 1 - B, BB backshift operator dd memory parameter. curves YtY_t follow functional autoregressive moving-average (FARMA) model orders pp qq, Yt(u)−∑=1p(ΦiYt−)(u)=ηt(u)+∑j=1q(Θjηt−j)(u),Y_t(u) - \sum_{=1}^{p} (\Phi_i Y_{t-})(u) = \eta_t(u) + \sum_{j=1}^{q} (\Theta_j \eta_{t-j})(u), autoregressive operators Φi\Phi_i, moving-average operators Θj\Theta_j innovations ηt\eta_t. farfima package fits model three steps. estimates dd, selects pp qq, estimates operators. forecasts curves conformal prediction bands. main functions : section introduces one function applies French female mortality rates.

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: farfima() fits model training sample three steps. First, estimates dd estimate_memory(). Second, centres fractionally differences training curves, drops first trim differenced curves, selects pp qq select_order(). Third, estimates operators functional Hannan-Rissanen method, estimate_operators(). validation sample, also forecasts h steps ahead every validation origin, uses forecast errors calibrate conformal prediction bands horizon level. main arguments : fit estimates dd BC-LPWN2, selects orders functional information criterion p,q∈{0,…,5}p, q \\{0, \dots, 5\}, calibrates SR, NS AC bands 80% 95% levels horizons 10 years. estimate dd 1.12. 0.5, curves non-stationary. selected model differenced curves FARMA(0, 1). fit list:

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: estimate_memory() estimates dd leading score process, centred curves projected onto leading eigenfunction covariance-type operator. estimators local Whittle ("lw"), detrended fluctuation analysis ("dfa"), local polynomial Whittle noise ("lpwn1", "lpwn2"), bias-corrected versions prefiltered sieve bootstrap ("bc_lpwn1", "bc_lpwn2"). m_const sets bandwidth, B number bootstrap samples. seed, BC-LPWN2 gives estimate used fit:
code: m = estimate_memory(blocks$train, method = "bc_lpwn2", seed = 1) m #> Memory estimate d = 1.12 #>   BC-LPWN2 on the leading score process of the empirical covariance operator (Covar), bandwidth exponent 0.75 #>   uncorrected d = 1.01, bootstrap bias = -0.11, bootstrap sd = 0.329 #>   note: the LPWN estimate is at the boundary of its search interval #>   note: 62% of the bootstrap estimates are at the boundary sapply(c("dfa", "lw", "lpwn1", "lpwn2"), function(meth) estimate_memory(blocks$train, method = meth)$d) #>       dfa        lw     lpwn1     lpwn2  #> 0.9740937 0.8948049 1.0100000 1.0100000

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: frac_diff() applies ∇d=(1−B)d\nabla^d = (1 - B)^d every grid point. farfima() centres training curves, fractionally differences d drops first trim. steps hand give short-memory curves y: negative d undoes differencing:
code: y = frac_diff(blocks$train - rowMeans(blocks$train), d = m$d)[, -(1:20)] dim(y) #> [1] 96 43 z = frac_diff(blocks$train, d = m$d) max(abs(frac_diff(z, d = -m$d) - blocks$train)) #> [1] 4.884981e-15

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: select_order() selects pp qq short-memory curves. "ic_full" minimises adaptive functional Hannan-Quinn information criterion candidates, "ic_auto" uses criterion stepwise search. "bj", functional Box-Jenkins method, tries candidates increasing p+qp + q stops first whose residuals pass functional portmanteau test. "cv" minimises forecast error validation sample. plot() shows criterion candidate, selected model boxed. "ic_auto" warns largest model unstable. smaller range avoids : order = "cv", farfima() selects orders forecasting validation curves original scale:
code: o_ic = select_order(y, method = "ic_full") o_ic #> Selected (p, q) = (0, 1) #>   functional IC (exhaustive search), 35 candidates select_order(y, method = "bj", seed = 1) #> Selected (p, q) = (1, 0) #>   functional Box-Jenkins, 20 lags, 35 candidates o_auto = select_order(y, method = "ic_auto") #> Warning: The largest candidate FARMA(5, 5) is unstable; use smaller ranges of p #> and q. select_order(y, method = "ic_auto", p = 0:3, q = 0:3) #> Selected (p, q) = (0, 1) #>   auto functional IC, 15 candidates fit_cv = farfima(blocks$train, blocks$valid, d = m$d, order = "cv", h = 5, trim = 20, verbose = FALSE) fit_cv$order #> p q  #> 1 0 oldpar = par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(o_ic) plot(fit_cv$order_selection) par(oldpar)

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: estimate_operators() estimates operators FARMA(p, q) model functional Hannan-Rissanen method. operator stored grid grid matrix, applying curve matrix product. plot() draws operators heatmaps, red positive blue negative values. selected orders, gives operators fit:
code: op = estimate_operators(y, order = o_ic) op #> FARMA(0, 1) operators #>   Data:      96 grid points x 43 curves #>   Operators: functional Hannan-Rissanen estimator with 1 principal component #>   Norms:     MA lag 1 = 0.427 all.equal(op[c("phi", "theta")], fit[c("phi", "theta")]) #> [1] TRUE plot(op, xlab = "Age v", ylab = "Age u")

title: farfima: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: sim_farfima() simulates n curves FARFIMA(p, d, q) model no_grid equally spaced points [0, 1], Brownian motion innovations. ar_strength ma_strength set operator norms. Simulated curves useful check methods true model known:
code: sim = sim_farfima(n = 500, d = 0.3, p = 1, q = 0, ar_strength = 0.5, seed = 1) sb = split_curves(sim) fit_sim = farfima(sb$train, sb$valid, d = "lpwn2", h = 5, trim = 50, verbose = FALSE) fit_sim$d #> [1] 0.5449465 fit_sim$order #> p q  #> 1 0

title: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: farfima provides tools modelling, forecasting visualising long-memory functional time series functional autoregressive fractionally integrated moving-average (FARFIMA) model. model fitted three steps, can also used . First, memory parameter estimated leading principal component scores, example local Whittle bias-corrected local polynomial Whittle noise. Second, autoregressive moving-average orders fractionally differenced curves selected functional information criterion, functional Box-Jenkins cross-validation. Third, operators estimated functional Hannan-Rissanen method. point forecasts come conformal prediction bands quantify uncertainty. Visualisation tools include improved rainbow plots plots fitted model forecasts.

title: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: farfima needs R 4.1.0 later. Installing also installs packages uses: FCVAR, far, ftsa, longmemo, rainbow, sde, vars, withr wwntests. examples vignette also use demography package.
code: # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("chang-liu-0122/farfima", build_vignettes = TRUE)

title: Order Selection and Forecasting in Long-Memory Functional Time Series
text: Curves stored matrix grid points rows time columns, ages years. fts objects rainbow ftsa packages also work. example uses French female mortality rates demography package, years 1901 2006, ages 0 94 group ages 95 . test evaluation reports RMSPE MAPE point forecasts, ECP, CPD, MIS WIS conformal prediction bands.
code: library(farfima) library(demography)  # French female log death rates fr = extract.ages(extract.years(fr.mort, 1901:2006), 0:95) x = log10(smooth.demogdata(fr, method = "mspline", b = 65, weight = TRUE)$rate$female) plot_curves(x)  # Training, validation and test samples blocks = split_curves(x, train = 0.6, valid = 0.2)  # Fit the model and calibrate the conformal prediction bands fit = farfima(blocks$train, blocks$valid, h = 10, level = c(0.8, 0.95), trim = 20, seed = 1) fit plot(fit, type = "residuals")  # Forecast, and evaluate on the test sample fc = predict(fit, test = blocks$test) fc plot(fc, h = 1, band = "AC", xlab = "Age", ylab = "log10 death rate")

title: Estimate the memory parameter — estimate_memory
text: x matrix curves (grid points time). method Estimator: "lw" (local Whittle), "dfa" (detrended fluctuation analysis), "lpwn1" "lpwn2" (local polynomial Whittle noise, one two polynomial correction terms), "bc_lpwn1" "bc_lpwn2" (BC-LPWN1 BC-LPWN2, LPWN estimate bias-corrected prefiltered sieve bootstrap). cov_type Operator FPCA gives leading eigenfunction: "sample" (empirical covariance operator), "lrc_RS" (long-run covariance operator adaptive bandwidth) "lrc_LRS" (long-run covariance operator sandwich form). m_const Bandwidth exponent \(\), \(\lfloor 1 + T^\rfloor\) frequencies used. B, burn_in Number bootstrap samples burn-length (BC-LPWN). R_noise Number polynomial terms noise LPWN. tuning_const Constant \(c\). score process differenced estimate least \(1 - c / \log m\). cov_band_const Bandwidth constant cov_type = "lrc_LRS". dfa_levels, dfa_minnpts, dfa_cutoff Number block sizes, minimum number points per block range block sizes DFA regression. seed Optional seed bootstrap. verbose Whether show progress.

title: Fit a FARFIMA model — farfima
text: train Training sample: matrix curves (grid points time) fts object. valid Validation sample, following train. needed conformal prediction bands order = "cv". d Memory parameter estimator estimate_memory() ("lw", "dfa", "lpwn1", "lpwn2", "bc_lpwn1" "bc_lpwn2"), known value. order Order selection method select_order() ("ic_full", "ic_auto", "bj" "cv"), known orders c(p, q). "cv", forecasts compared validation curves original scale. p, q Candidate AR MA orders searched selection method. used order gives orders. (0, 0) excluded. method "farma" functional Hannan-Rissanen estimator, "far" FAR(1) benchmark fitted far::far(). benchmark ignores order, d = 1 FARFIMA(1, 1, 0) benchmark. h Maximum forecast horizon conformal prediction bands order = "cv". valid needs least h + 1 curves. level Nominal coverage levels conformal prediction bands. band Conformal prediction bands calibrate: "SR" (scaled residual), "NS" (non-conformity score), "AC" (adaptive conformal), "PID" (conformal PID control, proportional-integral-derivative) "AcMCP" (autocorrelated multistep conformal). See predict(). window "expanding" "fixed" window forecast origin. fixed window length training sample. valid_eval Optional curves check validation forecasts , place valid. forecasts still made valid. Use model fitted smoothed curves bands calibrated raw curves. must size valid. Npc Number principal components operator estimator. trim Number initial fractionally differenced curves dropped order selection estimation. Defaults \(\min(100, \lfloor T/3   \rfloor)\), \(T\) number training curves. far_pve Proportion variance explained components FAR(1) benchmark. memory_args List arguments estimate_memory(), m_const B. order_args List arguments select_order(), n_lags alpha. eta_grid Candidate learning rates AC, PID AcMCP conformal prediction bands. One rate chosen band level, mean interval score second half validation sample. zeta_grid Candidate multipliers SR band. symmetric TRUE, AC PID bands symmetric point forecast. FALSE, lower upper edges calibrated separately, level \(\alpha/2\). SR NS bands always symmetric AcMCP band always asymmetric. integrate Whether PID AcMCP bands include integral term, widens band repeated -coverage narrows repeated -coverage. extreme, band becomes infinite empty. KI Scale integral term. Defaults largest absolute standardised validation residual horizon. scorecast Scorecaster PID band: "none", "naive" (latest observed score curve) "theta" (theta method: exponential smoothing past scores plus half linear trend). acmcp_regression Whether centre AcMCP band also uses regression scores shorter horizons. FALSE, MA(h - 1) forecast used. seed Optional seed BC-LPWN bootstrap white-noise test order = "bj". verbose Whether show progress messages progress bar.

title: Forecast from a FARFIMA fit — predict.farfima

title: Select the FARMA orders — plot.farfima_order
text: "ic_full" (functional IC) minimises adaptive functional Hannan-Quinn information criterion candidates. "ic_auto" (auto functional IC) uses adaptive functional Hannan-Quinn information criterion stepwise search starting models. noise level comes largest model. "bj" (functional Box-Jenkins) tries candidates increasing p + q stops first whose residuals pass functional portmanteau test. "cv" (cross-validation) minimises RMSPE, MAPE, forecasts validation origins, averaged horizons. candidate whose fit fails origin dropped.
